name: What is the difference between a bump-out addition and a full kitchen addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a bump-out addition and a full kitchen addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out extends your existing kitchen by a few feet without requiring a full foundation rebuild, whereas a full room addition creates a completely new, large structural wing on a new foundation. A bump-out is ideal if you only need room for a kitchen island, an expanded sink run, or a breakfast nook. It is typically faster to construct and less expensive. A full addition requires extensive foundation and roof framing, but it gives you maximum freedom to build a spacious, multi-zone kitchen and walk-in pantry from scratch.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out adds two to three feet of cantilevered or supported space for extra depth, while a full addition builds a completely new room on an expanded foundation.
